explain.say: Gases only pass through wet skin, so glands keep it coated in mucus. That is why frogs live in damp places and quickly dry out and suffocate in hot, dry air.

faq.q: Can frogs breathe through their skin?
faq.a: Yes. Frog skin is thin and packed with blood vessels, so oxygen soaks in and carbon dioxide passes out. Some frogs get much of their oxygen this way, and underwater they rely on it completely.
asks: How much do frogs breathe through skin?

faq.q: Why must frog skin stay wet?
faq.a: Oxygen has to dissolve in water before it can pass through skin. Mucus glands keep the skin moist; if it dries out, the frog cannot breathe through it and is in danger.
asks: Why do frogs live near water?

faq.q: How do frogs pump air into their lungs?
faq.a: A frog has no diaphragm. It draws air into its mouth through its nostrils, closes them, then raises the floor of its mouth to push the air down into its lungs. That is why its throat bobs.
asks: Why does a frog's throat move?

faq.q: Why are frogs harmed by pollution?
faq.a: Because chemicals and germs pass through their thin, breathing skin easily. A fungus called chytrid attacks frog skin and has wiped out many frog species around the world.

faq.q: Is there a frog with no lungs?
faq.a: Yes. The Bornean flat-headed frog, found in fast, cold, oxygen-rich streams, has no lungs at all and breathes entirely through its skin.
asks: Can a frog live without lungs?
Which frog breathes only through skin?

facts: Frogs exchange gases through their skin as well as their lungs, and rely on skin breathing underwater.
The Bornean flat-headed frog, Barbourula kalimantanensis, has no lungs.
